- The callable fallback predicate reproduced primary-then-fallback for 529 and propagated 401 without fallback; total failure preserved two ordered ModelHTTPError leaves in FallbackExceptionGroup.

- Result/shared RunUsage retained cumulative success and failure usage, but durable one-row-per-run logging is caller-owned.
- The event handler received PartStartEvent, FinalResultEvent, and PartEndEvent. capture_run_messages retained both responses and retry feedback, but persistence, opt-in behavior, final-failure-only selection, redaction, and newest-20 rotation remain caller-owned.

Next unresolved maintainer decision (`explicit maintainer decision required`): whether Pydantic AI or Rebar owns the structured-output retry loop. Either choice must preserve three total attempts, early success, deterministic repair/extraction, stop-reason fast-fail, cumulative usage, public failure translation, and final-failure-only artifact timing. This investigation does not make that policy choice.

Residual gaps: live provider SDK transport was intentionally excluded by the offline requirement and remains covered by transport tests; wall-clock liveness remains covered by the exact timeout tests cited in the note. Decision: use one operation-wide Pydantic request_limit shared by tool turns and output-validation retries, sized as the existing base request allowance plus the configured bounded output-retry allowance. comments.body: RP-01 cache-impact validation completed with live direct-Anthropic and Bedrock calls; no credential values were printed or persisted. Artifact: .joe-janitor/rp01-cache-live-probe.py; detailed table and analysis: .joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-research.md. Models: Anthropic claude-sonnet-4-6 and Bedrock us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Both providers returned identical cache/input counts. Current fresh-run agentic reask: retry cache read/write 2,384/1,821; aggregate input/read/write 8,133/2,384/5,743. Proposed same-run Pydantic retry with agentic cache settings: retry read/write 3,920/289; aggregate 8,135/3,920/4,209. Thus the retry read 1,536 more cached tokens (+64%) and wrote 1,532 fewer (-84%). ProcessHistory reduced a synthetic 5,000-character faulty assistant response to 2,013 characters; the retry still read all 3,920 tokens written by request one, proving that truncation after the prior user boundary did not invalidate the cached prefix. A Rebar-owned ModelRetry error was 63 characters; both assistant history and error text must remain bounded. On the single_turn settings arm, same-run retry read only the 2,448-token static system/schema span versus 2,384 for the fresh shape; there was no message-tail benefit. Design implication for pending D2: if same-run retries are approved, every retry-capable structured run must request Rebar existing provider-specific message-tail breakpoint even when outer execution_mode is single_turn. Cache reuse improves billed cache mix/latency but does not shrink context-window use; preserve limits and add long tool-history probes. No production code changed.
